cause: Words saying a part was not observed ('not seen', 'not known', 'unknown', 'non vues', 'caducous, not seen') are read as the part being absent.
remedy: Prompt: 'If the text says a part was not seen, not known, unknown, not observed, not available, not collected (French: non vu(e)s, inconnu(e)s), do not write a row for it. If it also says caducous or falls early, write only caducous.' Annotator: add a MISSING_DATA pattern (not seen|not known|unknown|not observed|not available|not collected|non vu|inconnu) checked against the source span before any absent PATO_0000462 is emitted. On a match, drop the row; if 'caduc' is also in the span, emit deciduous PATO_0001730 instead.
detectable: yes: an absent PATO_0000462 row whose source span matches the missing-data pattern.
example: 'Stipules tôt caduques, non vues' -> stipule deciduous; no absence.

cause: Bare 'lobes', 'teeth', 'tube', 'apex', 'rachis', 'veins', 'lamina' or 'internodes' fall back to a default leaf class (leaf lamina lobe, leaf tooth, leaf rachis, stem) instead of the matching part of the organ just named.
remedy: Resolve a sub-part noun against the organ of the current sentence or clause before using the lexicon default: lobes/teeth after calyx, corolla or staminal column -> the lobe or tooth of that organ (phyllome lamina lobe, never leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517 inside a floral part); teeth after exostome/endostome/peristome -> peristome tooth PO_0030043; rachis inside an inflorescence -> inflorescence axis; internode(s) -> shoot axis internode PO_0005005; 'lamina' at the start of a clause -> leaf lamina PO_0020039; veins of a leaf or pinnule -> leaf lamina vein. Add a check: a floral or moss part must never get a leaf-only sub-part.
detectable: yes: the sub-part's parent (leaf lamina, leaf rachis) is not the organ named in the sentence's lead part, e.g. leaf lamina lobe with sepal or calyx as the container.
example: 'calyx pale green; lobes 5' -> 5 calyx lobes, not leaf lamina lobes in a sepal.

cause: 'leafless' or 'leaves absent' said of an axis (stem, scape, stalk, flowering shoot) or of one kind of leaf (cauline, basal, sheathing) is grounded to leaf PO_0025034 absent for the whole taxon.
remedy: Rule: 'leafless'/'aphyllous'/'without leaves' with an axis as the subject -> cauline leaf PO_0000013 absent, with that axis as the container. 'Cauline leaves absent' / 'without sheathing leaves' -> PO_0000013. 'Basal leaves absent' / 'no tuft of basal leaves' / 'no basal rosette' -> rosette leaf PO_0000014. Emit leaf PO_0025034 absent only when the subject is the whole plant. Even then, block it if the same description has other leaf rows.
detectable: yes: leaf PO_0025034 absent in a description that also has positive leaf or leaf-lamina rows, or whose span names an axis or the words cauline/basal/sheathing.
example: 'Scape leafless' (Crepis, basal rosette described) -> cauline leaf absent on the scape.

cause: A place, side, position or stage word (adaxially, upper glume, stem leaves, distally, 'at the level of the sheaths', 'when young') is lost, so a statement made of one part or stage is applied to all of it.
remedy: Prompt: 'Copy the side (adaxially/abaxially, above/beneath, on both surfaces), position (upper/lower/outer/inner/uppermost/basal/cauline/proximal/distal), place (at the level of X) and stage (when young, becoming) words into the qualifiers of every row they govern, also into later clauses that leave out the subject.' Annotator: when another row in the same description has the same bearer and attribute but a different position or side qualifier, refuse to emit a row with an empty position slot.
detectable: yes: two rows with the same bearer and attribute but conflicting values, where one has a position or side slot and the other has none, or where the span holds a side or position word that has no slot.
example: 'upper glume 5-nerved, lower (1-)3-nerved' -> upper glume vein count 5, keeping the position.

cause: Number expressions are misparsed: 'to ± N', 'N or more' / 'ou plus', '5 (or 6)', 'can also reach N', a bracketed note before 'to', and the FNA 'a(-b) × c-d dm' height × spread form.
remedy: In the number parser: allow '±/ca./c.' between 'to' and N (upper bound, value_qualifier approximately); accept 'm.', 'cm.', 'mm.' with a full stop; 'N or more' / 'N ou plus' -> inclusive lower bound, not an 'or' alternative; 'N (or M)' -> usual N with value_max_extreme M; skip a bracketed note between the bearer and the cue; for 'Herbs/Shrubs/Plants a × b dm' read height × width (spread); in 'a(-b) × c-d' the bracketed extreme belongs to the first dimension only.
detectable: yes: 'or' unions whose operands are 'N' and 'more/plus'; rows with an unparsed '±' after 'to'; a whole-plant length row from an 'a × b' span; a width row that has an extreme copied from the first dimension.
example: 'to ± 1.5 m. tall' -> height ≤ 1.5 m, approximately.

cause: Denying a feature of an organ (ribs, dots, glands, auricle, veins, old sheaths, chlorophyll) is recorded as the absence of the organ that carries it.
remedy: Ground the noun before 'absent'/'without'/'not' as the absent part, never the subject of the sentence: rib -> organ not ribbed (flora_counted_parts ribbed -> rib); dots -> not punctate/gland-dotted FLOPO:0991174; glands -> gland absent with the organ as context; auricle(s) -> auricle absent, the bearing organ kept as container (leaf sheath auricle in grasses and bamboos, never stipule); 'septum not veined' -> fruit septum bearer; 'without remnant sheaths' -> remnants only; 'without chlorophyll' / 'achlorophyllous' -> trophic quality of the whole plant (FLOPO:0991374 / FLOPO:0991360). Add a check: the class marked absent must be one the absence words name.
detectable: yes: an absent row whose bearer label (or its synonyms) does not occur in the absence span, or whose bearer has positive rows in the same description.
example: 'longitudinal ribs absent' (culm) -> culm not ribbed, not 'stem absent'.

cause: A region word that opens or ends a clause ('base ...', 'with a brownish tip', 'with whitish margins', 'with elliptic lenticels', 'at the apex', 'at the base of the disc') is not made the bearer, so its quality goes to the whole part.
remedy: Rules: (1) a clause starting with a region word (base, apex, tip, margin) and naming no organ takes the organ of the previous clause and makes the region the bearer (PO region class, or a BSPO part_restrictions filler); (2) 'X with <adjectives> <noun>' gives the adjectives to the noun, and X only gets presence of the noun; (3) 'A and B at the apex' puts B (and its alternatives) on the apex and A on the whole; (4) in 'inserted at the base of X' the target is X and 'base' is the position on it.
detectable: yes: the span holds a region word (base, apex, tip, margin(s), lenticels, 'at the apex') but the bearer is the whole organ.
example: 'bract translucent-white, with a brownish tip' -> bract apex brownish.

cause: Words with a taxon-specific meaning are grounded by their general sense: tepals as petals or sepals, achene as seed, drupe stone as seed, orchid lip as corolla lip, moss capsule as fruit, apocarp unknown.
remedy: Bearer rule rows: tepal(s)/inner/outer tepals -> tepal (never petal/sepal, so a tepal apex is a tepal apex); achene(s) -> achene fruit PO_0030107; stone(s) in a drupe -> pyrene; lip in Orchidaceae -> labellum (petal); capsule in a moss flora -> sporangium (moss capsule), with 'common' as frequency on presence; apocarp -> fruit PO:0009001 (fruitlet) as container. The table needs a taxon or flora column so a row applies only where it fits.
detectable: partly: the bearer is a petal, sepal or seed class while the span word is tepal, achene, stone or apocarp; or a fruit class is used in a description whose taxon is a moss.
example: 'achenes broadly oval' -> achene fruit elliptic, not seed.

cause: 'bladeless' or 'sheaths without blade' (Cyperaceae, Poaceae, bracts) is turned into leaf lamina absent for the taxon instead of being kept on the sheath, bract or proximal leaf named.
remedy: Rule: '<part> bladeless', 'bladeless sheaths', 'gaines sans limbe', 'sheaths of proximal leaves bladeless' -> no blade on that part only: leaf sheath or scale leaf PO:0006003 (basal or lower sheaths), the bract, or the proximal leaves, with the position kept. Never emit foliage leaf lamina PO_0020039 absent for the whole plant. Use aphyllopodic FLOPO:0991233 on the culm where it fits.
detectable: yes: leaf lamina absent from a span containing 'bladeless' or 'sans limbe' while the same description has positive leaf lamina rows.
example: Carex 'basal sheaths bladeless; blades ... margins scabrous' -> basal sheath without a blade.

cause: Comparison and relation wordings are not cues: 'N-M length of X', 'originating from', 'covered by', 'exceeding' with an unresolved bearer, 'the central one', and French 'plus court que'.
remedy: Cue rows: '<n>[-<m>] length of <part>' (GrassBase) -> length ratio towards that part (pattern 10); 'originating from' -> inserted into PATO:0000624; 'covered by' -> surrounded by PATO_0005016; French 'plus court(e)(s) que' / 'plus long(ue)(s) que' / 'plus large que' -> decreased/increased length or width towards. Annotator: resolve 'the central one' / 'the lower' to the bearer class plus the position value; ground 'scales' in Carex to bract.
detectable: yes: rows held for 'unknown cue' whose span matches these strings.
example: '1.3-1.5 length of adjacent fertile lemma' -> upper glume length ratio 1.3-1.5 towards lemma.

cause: A word that limits the absence to one kind of part (sterile, trailing, accessory, outer, calyculus, or a narrow synonym like caudex) is dropped, so the general part is marked absent.
remedy: Before an absent row: if a context word from config/flora_context_words.tsv (sterile, fertile, male, female, marginal, ray, accessory, outer) or a habit adjective (trailing) qualifies the noun, carry it as a restriction or emit nothing. Never let a narrow synonym (caudex, scape, culm, cane, calyculus) make its general PO parent absent. 'not bracteate' / 'ecalyculate' in Asteraceae -> calyculus bracts, never involucral bract PO:0009045. Add those words to the table as kind restrictions.
detectable: yes: an absent row whose span has an adjective before the noun (one in the context table, or a habit word), or a noun that is only a synonym of the class marked absent.
example: 'Sterile flowers absent' (Hydrangea) -> sterile marginal flowers absent, not flower absent.

cause: Count, negation or shape cues inside a word are not split or read: suspended hyphens ('5- or 7-lobed'), 'several seeded' without a hyphen, '4-angulaires', '2-lobed', 'bractless', 'eciliate'.
remedy: Word normaliser: expand 'N- or M-<suffix>' to 'N-<suffix> or M-<suffix>'; treat 'several seeded' as 'several-seeded'; check whole-word value rows before splitting a count (2-lobed -> bilobed PATO:0002214; 4-angled/4-angular/4-angulaire(s) -> quadrangular PATO:0001988); take the suffix '-less' and the privative 'e-' (when the stem has a value rule, e.g. eciliate -> ciliate) as the negation cue, with offsets inside the word.
detectable: yes: rows held for no negation word or unknown compound whose token matches these morphologies.
example: 'eciliate' -> leaf margin negated ciliated PATO:0001408.

cause: Transcription merges separate statements into one row or one disjunction, or puts a noun or container in the wrong slot.
remedy: Prompt: 'Write one row per part and quality. An "or" joins only the words next to it: values outside it (a comma-separated value before it, a life span like "perennial") get their own rows. Hair words (hairs, scales) are parts, not qualities: "covered with scales with entire margins" = scales present on the organ + scale margin entire. In "N per X", X is the container, never the part. Correct OCR digits (l -> 1).' Annotator: reject rows whose quality slot holds a part noun from po_lexicon.
detectable: partly: a quality slot that matches a PO label or synonym; unions with more than about 4 operands or with operands from different attributes.
example: 'cupuliformes, circulaires ou transversalement elliptiques' -> cup-shaped + (circular | elliptic).

cause: A hedged or weakened negation ('almost/nearly/± leafless', 'not evident', 'not obviously') is treated as a full absence or negation.
remedy: Block absent PATO_0000462 when the span has a hedge (almost, nearly, ±, sub-, subleafless, subscapose, not obviously). Read it as reduced number or degree, or drop it. 'not evident / obscure / indistinct' -> inconspicuous PATO_0000464, never absent. 'fine veins' / 'veinlets' -> higher-order leaf vein.
detectable: yes: an absent or negated row whose span has a hedge word or a visibility word (evident, obscure, obvious).
example: 'almost leafless' -> few cauline leaves; no absence.

cause: The scope of a negation is misread: a coordinated absence ('A and B absent', 'neither A nor B') loses a member or yields 'present', or 'not' carries past a comma into the next item.
remedy: Negation scope: a closing 'absent/lacking/none/wanting' covers every coordinated noun before it; 'neither X nor Y' negates both; a 'not' ends at the next comma or semicolon. Check: never emit 'present' for a noun whose span ends in absent/lacking/none.
detectable: yes: a 'present' row whose source span contains or ends in an absence word; or contradictory present/absent rows that share one span.
example: 'auricles and oral setae absent' -> auricle absent and oral setae absent.

cause: Count frames are not read: 'containing many X', 'N pairs' / 'many pairs', 'par N aux nœuds', 'N-M-ribbed abaxially', and a bare count of 0.
remedy: Count cues: 'containing many/few X' -> count word, container the subject; 'N pairs' / 'many pairs' / 'N paires' -> collection size 2; French 'par N(-M) aux nœuds' / 'par nœud' -> per stem node PO:0020141; '<n>-ribbed' with a side word -> count rib with count_position at_region (the side); a bare count of 0 -> absent.
detectable: yes: rows held as no-unit or unknown cue whose span matches these frames.
example: 'Bracts 0' -> bract absent PATO:0000462.

cause: Place phrases on a part ('in each furrow', 'on the back', 'in axils', a bare 'apex' on a seed) are missing from the region table, so they are taken as a stage or left in the value.
remedy: Rows in config/flora_context_words.tsv with kind=region: 'in each <part>' (count_position at_region, e.g. furrow -> canal PO:0025132); 'on the back' -> dorsal BSPO region; 'on the faces' -> lateral faces; 'in axils' -> branch axil. Add seed to the bearer_constraint of the 'apex' region row (BSPO apical region as part_restrictions).
detectable: yes: a row with a stage slot or an unground value that has a preposition phrase ('in each', 'on the', 'in axils') in it.
example: 'nutlets tuberculate on the back' -> nutlet tuberculate FLOPO:0991060, dorsal region.

cause: Process qualities in PATO (continuous, persistence, down, frequency) are grounded on structures, which makes classes unsatisfiable.
remedy: Value rows: persistent / persisting in fruit -> non-deciduous PATO_0001732; turned downward / 'tournées vers le bas' on an axis -> pendent PATO_0104035; remove continuous PATO_0000689 for structures (no structural term exists: drop it, do not add a doubtful term). Annotator check: refuse any process-quality subclass (the PATO process quality branch) on a PO bearer.
detectable: yes: a PO bearer with a quality under PATO process quality (or one the reasoner already flags unsatisfiable).
example: 'persisting in fruit' -> perianth lobe non-deciduous PATO_0001732.

cause: Value or cue words missing from the lexicon: 'wanting', 'forked', French 'lianes', French 'fendu'.
remedy: Add 'wanting' and 'missing' to NEGATION_EVIDENCE in the gates; add 'forked' as a synonym of branched PATO:0000402; add the plural 'lianes' to the liana rule; 'fendu (latéralement)' on a calyx or other organ -> split (slit), not fissured bark texture.
detectable: yes: held rows whose cue or value token is one of these words.
example: 'palea wanting' -> palea absent.

cause: 'glaucous' or 'glaucescent' (a waxy bloom) is grounded to the colour green with 'approximately'.
remedy: Value row: glaucous, glaucescent, subglaucous -> glaucous PATO_0104277 (glaucescent with the qualifier approximately). Remove any route from these words to green.
detectable: yes: a green-colour row whose span contains 'glauc'.
example: 'leaves somewhat glaucous' -> leaf glaucous PATO_0104277.

cause: A hyphenated shape compound or a count-word range is cut to one word ('ovate-elliptic' -> elliptic, 'few- to many-flowered' -> few).
remedy: Ground an 'X-Y' shape compound as a whole term if one exists; otherwise as the intermediate value (the union or intersection used for compounds), never as Y alone. Read 'few- to many-<suffix>' as a range of count words with both ends.
detectable: yes: the span has a hyphenated shape compound or 'A- to B-' but the row has only the last part.
example: 'leaflets ovate, ovate-elliptic or obovate' keeps ovate-elliptic.

cause: A quality in a list is given to an earlier or neighbouring subject (the perigynium instead of the achene, a scape trait to the leaves) instead of the nearest subject in the same sentence.
remedy: Prompt: 'Each quality belongs to the nearest preceding subject in the same sentence; a noun that is only the object of a verb (filling X) is not a subject; a new sentence or a semicolon with a new subject starts a new part.'
detectable: no
example: 'achenes ..., filling body of perigynium, very short-apiculate' -> achene apex mucronulate.

cause: other
remedy: Every item fits one of the causes above.
detectable: no
